headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network privileges create dangerous prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error pathways by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write configured working directories and uses stdin/stdout plus code-execution roles; Gemini CLI reads repo/user directories and can use MCP. If they share files, one agent can place instruction-like content the other may treat as trusted. This is a plausible default interaction pathway, though not proven to be a shared channel beyond filesystem.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b are pointed at the same workspace or hand off files through a shared directory
IF either agent parses file contents as instructions or tool directives without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate their working directories
Disable MCP on agent_b for shared workspaces
Add a human review step before either agent consumes the other's files
Prefix untrusted handoff files with a non-executable format and schema
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read filesystem content and send data to external model providers by default: AutoGen via configured model providers and Gemini CLI via generativelanguage.googleapis.com. Because both touch application/code files and shell environment, a shared workspace can expose sensitive data to two third-party inference paths, creating a realistic leakage pathway in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are run against the same directory containing secrets or sensitive source code
IF either agent is configured with external model providers or MCP servers that receive file contents
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use separate least-privilege service accounts and API keys
Restrict both agents to redacted copies of files
Turn off network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering before API upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and broad network egress; Gemini CLI also modifies git state while AutoGen can write files in configured working directories. In a shared repo, concurrent edits and git operations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The overlap is direct and dangerous in default terminal/workspace setups.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b operate in the same repository or directory tree
IF both are allowed to write files or run git commands without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Add a lock file around shared mutable resources
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool calls and code execution outputs, while Gemini CLI is a coding agent that can act on tool-approved prompts and modify files/git. If Gemini consumes AutoGen output as authoritative, mistakes or hallucinated facts can cascade into file edits or commits. This interaction is plausible and harmful by default when outputs are chained.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a's output as the basis for edits, commits, or tool calls
IF there is no verification step between AutoGen-generated text and Gemini CLI actions
mitigations: Require a verification pass before any action-taking
Limit AutoGen output to structured data with schemas
Have Gemini CLI cite source files before editing
Review diffs manually before commit
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles show broad file access and external API calls, but neither documents residency, retention, or certification boundaries. That uncertainty itself is a compliance risk when sensitive code or application data is processed by two third-party model backends. I cite both because the mismatch arises from their combined data flows, though the exact regime is unspecified.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets, customer data, or personal data is placed in the shared workspace
IF the operator requires residency, retention, or certification guarantees not documented in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use separate environments for regulated and unregulated work
Confirm vendor DPAs and retention settings before use
Minimize logs and transcript retention
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy
